title: A date and time a form sends carries its UTC offset
intent: A browser's local date-and-time control hands the page a wall time with no UTC offset. That names no instant: ten in the morning is a different moment in every zone. Sent as it is, the API refuses it for a timestamp, and a server that read it as UTC instead would store a person in any other zone off by their offset. So a form never sends the control's own value: it shows the instant in a zone and sends what is picked as the instant it names, with that zone's offset.
reference: Any JSX `type` attribute whose value is `datetime-local` is refused, on `Input`, a raw `input` or a wrapper that passes it on, in any letter case (the browser reads the type case-insensitively), as a string, an expression or a plain template. The reference stack ships `DateTimeInput` from `@terpjs/react-core`: it shows an RFC 3339 instant as wall time in a zone, the browser's own or one it is given, and sends what is picked as an RFC 3339 instant with that zone's offset; a wall time the clocks skip moves past the gap, and one they repeat is the earlier. A calendar day (`type="date"`) and a time of day (`type="time"`) name no instant and are not this rule's concern. The runtime half is the server's: a BaseSchema refuses timestamp text without an offset with a 422 (ADR 0206). A field that truly holds a wall time with a named zone, read as text by the API, keeps the control with the marker and its reason.

runtime.rationale: The server holds the invariant: a request body refuses timestamp text without a UTC offset with a 422 at its field, so a wall time sent from this control is refused where it enters instead of stored off by the sender's offset. The build-time half moves that refusal from the first request in production to the line the control is written on, and names the control that sends an instant instead.
